newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Bank director sees 2.5 pct Aug inflation.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Bank director sees 2.5 pct Aug inflation.

text.p: Venezuela's monthly inflation rate will likely increase slightly to 2.5 percent in August, from 1.8 percent in June, but will not rise above three percent per month in the foreseeable future, a top Central Bank official said.
"For August maybe there will be a rebound to 2.5 percent. This is well within the anti-inflation policy limits," Central Bank Director Domingo Maza Zavala told local Union Radio in an interview.
The Central Bank is due to announce the monthly and accumulated inflation rate for July later on Friday.
Maza did not comment on what that figure might be although markets are expecting it to come in slightly above June's 1.8 percent rate which was the second lowest monthly price rise for five years.

Maza said salary increases and higher services costs would push up the rate of inflation over the coming months, but added that "the inflation rate will never reach three percent in the next few months."
The Venezuelan government set its target for 1997 inflation to fall to between 30 and 35 percent from 103.2 percent in 1996.
Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said recently that the inflation target was attainable, based on the accumulated inflation rate of 14.6 percent over the first half of the year.
